baseline_10.title: Baseline, 10 nodes
baseline_10.summary: A small, healthy mesh: the reference for every other scenario.

collapse_40.title: Collapse, 40 nodes
collapse_40.summary: Forty nodes at 20% loss. A relay on the active path dies at t=10, the gateway at t=25 (every SOS must queue), and the gateway returns at t=60 (they must flush).

no_gateway.title: No gateway
no_gateway.summary: No node has an uplink. SOS messages are retained in store-and-forward until a rescue team walks into range at t=45, then everything flushes at once.

high_loss.title: High loss
high_loss.summary: Twenty nodes with 35% loss on every link: ACK, retry and rerouting under stress.

chain_10hop.title: Ten-hop chain
chain_10hop.summary: A single line of eleven nodes: the longest path the TTL of 10 allows.

hopcount_vs_weighted.title: Weighted vs hop-count routing
hopcount_vs_weighted.summary: Same topology, same seeds, same traffic, two routers. The short path crosses a lossy link; the long path is clean. Messages are best-effort, so a bad choice shows up directly as lost messages.

priority_load.title: SOS under load
priority_load.summary: A slow radio (one packet per 80 ms) and a burst of routine traffic, all heading for the same gateway: does an SOS still overtake it at every hop?
